Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed by the latency numbers. We want to move from evaluation to a formal Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so we can lock dates for an internal pilot. A few constraints up front:

- Data classification: pilot will include PHI-derived telemetry; we need HIPAA controls and either a Dedicated or Private deployment. Hosted (multi-tenant) is acceptable only if we can isolate data via dedicated capacity + contractual controls.
- Region/residency: primary customer data must remain in the US (us-east preferred).
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 and an operational runbook / audit logs required for procurement.

Target schedule from our side: decision on hosting mode by 2026-08-30, pilot start by 2026-09-15, go-live (full prod) by 2026-10-31. Can you draft a MAP and call out the delta between Dedicated vs Private (timeline, cost, blockers)?

Also curious about a short POC: 2 weeks with a small dataset and a standard prompt set to validate latency and hallucination rates. Can you confirm token quotas / trial access?

Sara

Summary recommendations (short version):
- Hosted (fastest): 0–2 weeks to spin a sandbox on our hosted API in us-east. Good for early eval but not recommended for PHI unless you take Dedicated capacity + BAA + additional contractual safeguards.
- Dedicated (recommended middle ground): 2–4 weeks for reserved GPU pools, predictable latency, and data isolation. Supports SOC 2 controls and can be configured with tenant-level audit logs. Best fit if you want faster time-to-prod with contractual data isolation.
- Private (on-prem / VPC): 6–10+ weeks depending on networking (Direct Connect / VPN) and HSM/KMS integration. Highest compliance assurance but the longest lead time and heavier ops footprint.

POC ask: we can offer a 2-week hosted token allotment for evaluation while we provision Dedicated for the pilot if you decide to go that route. Pricing delta and SOW language are noted in the attached MAP draft.

1) Quick alignment call (I can do Thu 8/20 10–11am PT) — invite sent.

3) SE deep-dive to confirm networking and any HSM/KMS needs.

Sara / team — quick technical context to help your evaluation: some practical tradeoffs we see when customers choose Dedicated vs Private for PHI workloads.

If you want the short table:
- Hosted (sandbox): fastest, no infra changes. Limitations: shared runtime (but we can allocate Dedicated capacity on top), limited control over networking/HSM. Good for early model validation.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in our us-east region, tenant-level audit logs, stronger isolation. Supports customer-managed KMS via keys-in-use or bring-your-own KMS (approx +2–3 weeks to configure keys and validate).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control over network boundary and key material; requires environment checklist: NAT/route tables, peering/Direct Connect, certs for mutual TLS, and (if air-gapped) an appliance install. Expect infra prep and acceptance testing to add 4–8 weeks.

Concrete asks for your security team before we can finalize estimates:
- Does Polaris require HSM-backed key storage or will a managed KMS with strict IAM meet requirements?
- Will you allow a staging dataset with token-level redaction for the POC?
- Any IP restrictions or approved subnets for egress?

Rough lead-time (ballpark):
- Hosted sandbox + token allotment: 48–72 hours
- Dedicated capacity (provision + KMS integration): 10–21 days
- Private deployment (VPC/direct-connect + acceptance): 6–10 weeks

I'll prepare a short appendix to the MAP that rows these options with cost and lead times; putting that in Vivek's MAP draft.

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
